scope: Infinitesimal test signals in the dynamical companion field from the prior closed Hamiltonian. Distinguish signal strength from radiation loading; test carrier/arrival-time mapping and finite-event distortion. No astronomical inference.
equations: Independently integrate Hamilton rays dx/dt=1/n, dk/dt=k*n_x/n^2 and the arrival variational system dt/dx=n, dJ/dx=n_t*J. Initialize k=nu_emitted*n_emitted. Compare nu_emitted/nu_received to J.
energy_scope: Test photons are infinitesimal and do not drive the background. Their finite energy must not be added to a conservation claim for the background solution. The previous full Hamiltonian result establishes transfer with backreaction; this test establishes its weak-signal propagation limit.
clock_controls: Report reference-clock factor J and alternative measured factors J*(n_emitted/n_received)^p for atom-frequency scaling q(n)=n^-p, p=0,1,2. These are conditional comparisons, not an adoption of a matter-clock law.
limits: One localized driving packet and a periodic scalar field are not a realistic ambient radiation population or a void/galaxy environment. Uniform initial rolling motion is prescribed as an initial state, not derived cosmological history. A short-event local stretch need not give an affine map over a long event. Weak-signal source independence is a limit, not a finite-brightness calibration.
